label: prop:canonical-closure-torus-chain
title: The canonical closure is a chain of $(2,\mathrm{odd})$-torus knots: bridge number $2A+1$ and total curvature $2\pi(2A+1)$
html:
Resolve each averaged letter of the canonical word of the atomic braid to a crossing sign (either branch) and freely reduce. The result is a chain form

  W_A \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{A-1} \sigma_{3k}^{\,a_k}\,\sigma_{3k+1}^{\,b_k}\,\sigma_{3k+2}^{\,\varepsilon_k}
  \qquad(\text{no } \varepsilon \text{ on the last block}),

each generator appearing exactly once, in order, as a single power, with a_k odd, b_k even and non-zero, and \varepsilon_k = \pm 1. Consequently its closure is the linear connected sum of the torus links T(2, e_i) along shared strands: A knots T(2, a_k) and one unknot, consecutive components linked with \mathrm{lk} = b_k/2; the A-1 interface generators are connected-sum bands with the unknot and drop out, leaving the (2A+1)-strand chain W'_A = \prod_k \sigma_{2k}^{a_k}\sigma_{2k+1}^{b_k} with the same closure. Hence

  \mu = A+1,\qquad \#\{\text{knotted components}\} = A,\qquad b(L) = 2A+1,
  \qquad \inf_{\text{isotopy class}} \int \kappa\, ds \;=\; 2\pi\,(2A+1).

The exponents

Read off the canonical interface composition block by block (verified for every isotope through A = 12 on both branches):

a_k (generator 3k) b_k (generator 3k+1) \varepsilon_k (interface 3k+2)
averaged \to \sigma 7 for every nucleon -2 (proton), -4 (neutron) +1 (pp), -1 (nn), +1 (pn)
averaged \to \sigma^{-1} 5 (proton), 3 (neutron) -4 for every nucleon +1 (pp), -1 (nn), -1 (pn)

So on the \sigma branch every knotted component is T(2,7); on the \sigma^{-1} branch protons give T(2,5) and neutrons T(2,3). The linking graph is the path with \mathrm{lk}(k, k+1) = b_k/2 \in \{-1, -2\}, the sublinks of consecutive pairs are not (2, 2\,\mathrm{lk})-torus links, and the components are not unknots -- which is a second, independent reason the Borromean (Brunnian) picture does not describe this closure.

Proof

Chain form. Each nucleon block uses generator 3k seven times and generator 3k+1 four times, in that order, and the interface to the next block is the single generator 3k+2; resolving and freely reducing gives the table.

Connected sum. A closed braid whose word is a product of sub-words on strand sets overlapping in exactly one strand is the connected sum of the closures of the sub-words along that strand [birman1974]; iterating gives the linear chain of T(2, e_i). Since T(2, \pm 1) is the unknot and a connected sum with the unknot is the identity, each \sigma_{3k+2}^{\pm 1} can be deleted and the indices closed up: W'_A has the same closure.

Bridge number. A closed n-braid is an n-bridge presentation, so b(L) \le 2A+1. Each T(2, a_k) with a_k \ge 3 odd has bridge number 2 and the unknot has 1; bridge number is at least the sum over components, so b(L) \ge 2A + 1.

Curvature. Milnor [milnor1950]: the infimum of total curvature over an isotopy class equals 2\pi times the bridge number. (Under Crofton, total curvature is \pi times the average number of critical points of the height functions -- the oscillation count, integrated -- which is where the serpenoid picture that prompted this result becomes exact.)

What is formalised, what is checked, what is cited

QOU.Mass.TorusKnotPages (sorry-free) carries the algebra: the Seifert form of T(2,n) is unimodular for every odd n; the continuant of V - X V^{\mathsf T} satisfies (X+1) D_{2g} = X^{2g+1} + 1, so the Alexander polynomial is (X^n+1)/(X+1) and divides X^{2n}-1; the floor 2A+1 \le b \le 3A is bookkeeping from \mu = A+1 and A knotted components (curvature_floor). The chain form and its exponents are verified exactly for A \le 12, and the symbolic predictions -- components, knot types, linking, and that W'_A closes to the same link (Jones polynomial and per-component Jones) -- for A \le 4, by the_canonical_closure_is_a_chain_of_torus_links_probe.py; the computational instance at A \le 6 via Reidemeister simplification and Vogel's algorithm is the_curvature_floor_is_sharp_probe.py. Not formalised: the two topological facts above, Milnor's theorem, and the identification of the components from their Jones polynomials.

Scope

Everything here is per classical branch: the canonical Hecke element is not a link, its 2A+1 averaged letters have no crossing sign, and a statement about the un-resolved object does not exist. Nothing here connects curvature to binding, and nothing supplies the twist: the osculating circle sees \kappa and is blind to \tau, and the framing datum the binding gap needs lives in the torsion.
